授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（日本語）: 本コースでは、剛体の回転力学、ならびにトルクと角運動量の複雑な力学的挙動を分析することで、物理系を支配する根本的な法則を探究する。弾性と静的平衡の観点から物質の構造的限界を検討する一方で、周期運動に固有のリズミカルなエネルギー移動をモデル化する。さらに、高速度域における時間、空間、および質量の相対論的変化を考察することで、概念的な視野を広げる。これらの領域を通じて、微積分は物理的直観を深化させ、高度な実世界の諸問題を解決するために必要な分析的精度を研ぎ澄ますための不可欠なツールとして活用される。
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.授業科目の目的（英語）: In this course, students explore the fundamental laws governing physical systems by analyzing the mechanics of rigid body rotation and the complex dynamics of torque and angular momentum. They examine the structural limits of materials through the lens of elasticity and static equilibrium, while modeling the rhythmic energy transfers inherent in periodic motion. Furthermore, learners broaden their conceptual horizons by investigating the relativistic shifts in time, space, and mass at high velocities. Throughout these topics, the use of calculus serves as a vital tool to deepen physical intuition and sharpen the analytical precision required to solve sophisticated real-world problems.
授業科目の目的・目標・履修条件について.キーワード: Rotational motion, simple harmonic motion, relativity, elasticity, equilibrium

head: 授業のテーマ
授業の内容（90分授業＝2時間）
事前/事後学修の内容
rows: Review on the concept of mechanics
Vectors, motion in one and two Dimensions, Newton's laws of motion, work and kinetic energy, potential energy and energy conservation, momentum, impulse and collisions, gravitation

Angular velocity and acceleration, rotation with constant angular acceleration, relating linear and angular kinematics, energy in rotational motion, parallel-axis theorem, moment of inertia calculations
Torque, torque and angular acceleration for a rigid body, rigid-body rotation about a moving axis, work and power in rotational motion, angular momentum conservation of angular momentum

Describing oscillation, simple harmonic motion, energy in simple harmonic motion, applications of simple harmonic motion, the simple pendulum, the physical pendulum, damped oscillations, forced oscillations and resonance

Invariance of physical laws, relativity of simultaneity, relativity of time intervals, relativity of length, the Lorentz transformations, relativistic momentum, work and energy, Newtonian mechanics and relativity
Conditions of equilibrium, center of gravity, solving rigid-body equilibrium problems, stress, strain, elastic moduli, elasticity and plasticity
